messages.content: Our AR-200 on the palletizing cell threw torque fault T-14 on J3 three times since 6am. We cleared it each time but it keeps coming back. Can you help? This is Brookvale Stamping, plant 2.

Hi Jonah, three T-14 faults in one shift means we treat this as a line-down ticket, so I've upgraded it to P1 and paged Dana Okafor's field team.
1. Stop that arm now and leave the CellBrain powered so the logs are kept.
2. Export the fault bundle: CellBrain > Diagnostics > Export Bundle, and reply with the .cbx file plus the arm serial.
3. This pattern usually means a worn joint 3 harmonic drive [AR2-HD-J3]; as a Premier account you get a technician on site within 8 hours, and I'm starting the RMA so the part ships today.
Line status: the palletizing arm must stay stopped, but your other cells on separate controllers can keep running.
hi, any update on RMA-AR-4471? we sent the fault bundle on monday and havent heard back

Hi, thanks for checking in. RMA-AR-4471 was approved Tuesday morning and the replacement encoder [AR2-ENC-04] shipped from Harrow Park depot by overnight freight; it should be with you today.
1. When it arrives, keep the box and the prepaid return label inside.
2. Send the failed encoder back within 15 calendar days so it isn't billed at list price.
Line status: per your ticket the arm is re-homed and running, so the line can keep running until the swap.
The screen on our TP-9 teach pendant keeps going black for a few seconds when the operator moves around the cell. Feels like a cable thing?

That does sound like the pendant cable rather than the pendant itself.
1. Check the cable along its length for pinches or kinks, especially where it passes the cell door.
2. Reseat the connector at the CellBrain and tighten the locking ring.
3. If the blackouts continue, we'll send a replacement 5 m cable [TP-9-CBL5] ($180, or covered if the controller is in warranty).
Line status: the line can keep running in automatic mode; just avoid jogging the arm by hand while the screen is unreliable.
We're on firmware 4.6.3 across four CellBrains. Do we have to move to 4.7.2 right away or can it wait until our shutdown in December?

It can wait. Rail 4.6.x is supported until 31 March 2027, so a December update is fine.
1. Plan about 25 minutes per controller with each CellBrain in Maintenance mode.
2. Back up every program as a .cbp file before you start.
3. Update one controller first, run a test cycle, then do the other three.
Line status: no action needed now; the line can keep running on 4.6.3.
How do I order more of the 40mm suction cups for the Gripkit vacuum head? Ours are getting torn.

You'll want the Gripkit 40 mm vacuum cups [GK-VAC-40], sold in 10-packs at $68.
1. Reply with the quantity and your ship-to address, or order through your account portal.
2. They ship by parcel from Millbrook depot, usually the next business day.
3. Note that vacuum cups are wear parts, so they are not covered under the Gripkit warranty.
Line status: torn cups lose grip on lighter parts, but the line can keep running if you swap the worst cups from your spares.
AR-60 cobot on line 3 went into fault S-12 after a worker brushed against it. Now it won't reset. We need it back ASAP.

S-12 is a safety skin fault, so we have to handle it carefully.
1. Inspect the safety skin pads for cracks or a loose pad; a damaged pad keeps S-12 active.
2. Press the reset on the pendant only after the area is clear and the pads are intact.
3. If a pad is damaged, we'll ship a replacement safety skin pad [AR6-SKIN-02] from Harrow Park depot.
4. Send the fault bundle (CellBrain > Diagnostics > Export Bundle) so we can confirm it was a real contact and not a sensor fault.
Line status: that cobot's cell must stay stopped until S-12 clears; do not bypass the skin. Cells on separate safety circuits can keep running.
CellBrain in cell 5 is showing warning W-22 and the fan is really loud. Its in a hot corner of the plant.

W-22 is the CellBrain over-temperature warning, and a loud fan usually means it's worn out.
1. Clear any dust from the intake grille and make sure there's at least 10 cm of clearance around the cabinet.
2. Order a replacement fan [CB-FAN-2] ($95); it's a 10-minute swap with the controller powered down.
3. If W-22 stays on after cleaning, schedule the fan swap for your next break.
Line status: W-22 is a warning, not a fault, so the line can keep running, but if it escalates to a temperature fault the controller will stop the cell.
Power went out last night. Since restart, two of our AR-200s say E-07 and won't move.

E-07 is an encoder mismatch and it's very common after a power loss.
1. On each affected arm, run the homing routine from the teach pendant.
2. If the arm homes cleanly, the E-07 clears and you can resume.
3. If E-07 comes back after homing, send the fault bundle; that points to a failed encoder [AR2-ENC-04] and we'll open an RMA.
Line status: the two arms stay stopped until they home cleanly; all other arms can keep running.
We keep getting C-31 on the CellBrain for the packaging cell, maybe once an hour. The robot stops and the PLC loses it.

C-31 is a fieldbus timeout between the CellBrain and your PLC.
1. Check the fieldbus cable for damage and make sure the connectors at both ends are seated.
2. Confirm the bus is terminated at the last device; a missing terminator causes exactly this intermittent pattern.
3. If it keeps happening, export a fault bundle so Marcus Lindqvist on our CellBrain team can check the timing logs.
Line status: other cells can keep running; the packaging cell can run too, but expect stops until the bus is fixed.
what does it cost to move from CareGuard Standard to Premier? we have 9 arms

CareGuard Premier is $5,800 per arm per year versus $2,400 on Standard, so for 9 arms that's $52,200 a year (a difference of $30,600).
1. Premier adds an on-site technician within 8 hours on line-down tickets (48 hours on Standard).
2. Advance replacements ship same day when the RMA is approved before 14:00 CT.
3. You also get a loaner CellBrain (up to 30 days), quarterly firmware reviews and a named customer success manager.
Line status: this is an account question, so nothing changes on your line.
Our AR-60 was delivered 14 months ago and now the hand guiding button doesn't do anything. Is that warranty?

Unfortunately the AR-60 cobot warranty is 12 months from ship date, so at 14 months it's out of warranty unless you have a CareGuard plan.
1. First, check the hand-guiding setting is enabled on the pendant under Collaborative settings; a firmware update can reset it.
2. If it is enabled and still dead, send a fault bundle and we'll quote the repair.
3. If you're on CareGuard Standard or Premier, the repair is covered under the plan.
Line status: hand-guiding is only used for teaching, so the line can keep running in automatic mode.
We got an invoice for $3,400 for a harmonic drive we DID return. The tracking shows it arrived. Please fix this.

Sorry about that. A $3,400 charge is the list price of the joint 3 harmonic drive [AR2-HD-J3], which is only billed if the core isn't received within 15 days.
1. Reply with the RMA number and the return tracking number.
2. I'll ask Priya Halvorsen on the RMA desk to match the receipt at Harrow Park depot.
3. Once it's matched, the invoice is cancelled and you'll get a credit note within 2 business days.
Line status: this is a billing issue only; your line can keep running.
LINE DOWN. both arms in cell 1 stopped, controller wont boot. calling hotline too

We have you. This is logged as a P1 line-down ticket and Dana Okafor's team is calling you back within the hour.
1. Check the CellBrain power LED; if it's dark, check the 48 V supply output.
2. If the supply is dead, the likely part is the CellBrain power supply [CB-PSU-48] and we'll start an advance replacement right away.
3. Don't swap boards or reflash anything until the technician is on the line.
Line status: cell 1 cannot run until the controller boots; other cells on their own CellBrains can keep running.
The quick change plate on our Gripkit two finger gripper has a bit of play in it. Is that normal?

No, the quick-change plate [GK-QC-1] should have no play once locked.
1. Remove the tool and check the locking pins for wear or debris.
2. Re-lock and check again; if there's still play, the plate needs replacing ($240, ships from Millbrook depot).
3. After any swap, re-check the tool center point on the pendant.
Line status: you can keep the line running at reduced speed for now, but replace the plate before the play gets worse and parts start dropping.
Can we get on-site training for our new operators? We have 6 people starting next month.

Yes. On-site training is $1,450 per day for up to 8 trainees, so your 6 operators fit in one session.
1. Have them take CellBrain Operator 101 first; it's remote and free for CareGuard customers.
2. Reply with three possible dates and your plant address.
3. We'll confirm a trainer and send the agenda within 2 business days.
Line status: training is scheduled around production, so the line can keep running.
What payload should I enter on the pendant? Our gripper is 2.1 kg and the boxes are up to 8 kg.

Enter the combined weight: 2.1 kg tool plus 8 kg box gives 10.1 kg, which is within the AR-200's 12 kg max payload.
1. On the teach pendant, open Tool settings and set payload to 10.1 kg.
2. Set the center of gravity offset for the heaviest box, not the average.
3. Run one slow test cycle with a full box.
Line status: the line can keep running; a wrong payload setting is the most common cause of torque fault T-14, so this is worth doing now.
Robot crashed into a fixture during a changeover. Collision detection was turned off because it kept false-tripping. J2 now makes a grinding noise. Covered under Premier right?

I'm sorry to say this one isn't covered. Crash damage while collision detection was disabled is excluded under every plan, including Premier.
1. Stop the arm; a grinding J2 usually means a damaged harmonic drive [AR2-HD-J2] (list $3,850).
2. Send the fault bundle and we'll confirm the part and send a quote.
3. Your Premier on-site visit is still within 8 hours, and labor stays covered by the plan.
4. Before restart, re-enable collision detection; Marcus Lindqvist can help tune it so it stops false-tripping.
Line status: that arm must stay stopped until J2 is inspected; other cells can keep running.
We still run firmware 3.9 on an older CellBrain. Is there a patch for the pendant freeze bug?

Rail 3.x is end-of-life, so there are no more patches for 3.9, including that freeze bug.
1. The fix is in rail 4.x; the current stable is 4.7.2.
2. Back up all programs (.cbp) and plan about 25 minutes in Maintenance mode for the update.
3. If you plan to use TP-9 pendants, they need rail 4.5 or later anyway.
Line status: the line can keep running on 3.9 for now, but plan the update at your next scheduled stop.
Our CellBrain died and we're on the Standard plan. Can we get a loaner controller while it's repaired?

Loaner CellBrain controllers are a Premier-only benefit, so we can't send one on Standard.
1. On Standard, the advance replacement controller ships from Harrow Park depot the next business day after RMA approval.
2. Send the fault bundle if the controller still boots far enough to export it, or the serial number if not.
3. Your on-site technician window for a line-down ticket is 48 hours, but most controller swaps are done remotely with your maintenance team.
Line status: the cell on that controller is down until the replacement arrives; other cells can keep running.
Third RMA this month at our Ashby site, we need another advance replacement for an encoder. Two are still open. Can you just send it?

I want to get this moving, but a third open advance replacement at one site needs approval from your customer success manager.
1. I've sent the request to Teodora Vance with your RMA details; approvals usually come back within a few hours.
2. Meanwhile, if you can return either of the two open cores, the limit frees up and we can ship immediately.
3. Please include the fault bundle for the new encoder [AR2-ENC-04] so the RMA is ready the moment it's approved.
Line status: the affected arm stays stopped until it homes cleanly; the rest of the line can keep running.
How often do we need to grease the joints on the AR-200? Maintenance team is asking.

Grease J1 to J3 every 4,000 operating hours.
1. Use one joint grease cartridge [AR2-GRS-1] per joint ($45 each).
2. Do it with the arm powered down and locked out.
3. Log the hours on the pendant so the next service reminder is correct.
Line status: greasing takes the arm offline for about an hour, so do it at a planned stop; otherwise the line can keep running.
is the AR-60 reach long enough to reach a conveyor 1.1m away from the base

No, the AR-60 cobot has a 900 mm reach, so 1.1 m is out of range.
1. Move the base closer so the pick point is well inside 900 mm, or
2. Use the AR-200, which reaches 1,450 mm (12 kg payload), though it isn't a cobot and needs guarding.
3. Send us a layout drawing and we'll check the cell.
Line status: this is a planning question; your current line keeps running.
How do I get the fault bundle off the CellBrain? Support keeps asking for it.

Here's how to export it.
1. On the CellBrain screen or teach pendant, go to Diagnostics > Export Bundle.
2. Insert a USB stick when prompted; the file saves as a .cbx file with the controller serial in the name.
3. Email the .cbx file to acme.support@example.com with your ticket number.
Line status: exporting does not stop the robot, so the line can keep running while you do it.
We lost the prepaid return label for RMA-AR-3920. The box got thrown out too.

No problem, I'll get you a new label.
1. I've asked the RMA desk to email a new prepaid label to you within the hour.
2. Any sturdy box with padding is fine; mark the RMA number on the outside.
3. Ship it to Harrow Park depot by the 15th day after the replacement arrived, or the part will be billed at list price.
Line status: this doesn't affect production; your line can keep running.
Where do we send the broken Gripkit vacuum head back to? The RMA paper says Harrow Park but someone told me different.

Good catch. Gripkit parts go back to Millbrook depot, not Harrow Park.
1. Use the prepaid label from the replacement box; Gripkit labels are already addressed to Millbrook.
2. If your label says Harrow Park, reply with the RMA number and I'll have a corrected label sent.
3. Return it within 15 calendar days of receiving the replacement.
Line status: if the replacement head is installed, the line can keep running.
The jaws on our GK-2F-110 gripper don't close evenly anymore. One side lags.

An uneven close on the two-finger gripper [GK-2F-110] is usually the finger pads or the jaw guide.
1. Check the finger pads; worn pads [GK-PAD-6] ($54 per 6-pack) cause exactly this and aren't covered by warranty.
2. Clean the jaw guide rails and cycle the gripper 10 times from the pendant.
3. If it still lags, send a short video and the serial; within the 6-month Gripkit warranty we'll replace it.
Line status: the line can keep running at reduced speed, but watch for dropped parts.
CellBrain won't power on, power supply light is off. We think the PSU is gone.

That points to the CellBrain 48 V power supply [CB-PSU-48].
1. Check the input breaker and mains feed to the cabinet first.
2. If mains is fine and the PSU LED stays off, we'll ship a replacement PSU ($780 list, covered if the controller is inside its 36-month warranty).
3. Reply with the controller serial and we'll open an RMA right away.
Line status: every arm on that CellBrain is stopped until the PSU is replaced; this is a line-down ticket, so we've set it to P1.
The new TP-9 pendant just shows connecting... and never connects to our CellBrain. The old pendant works fine.

The TP-9 needs firmware rail 4.5 or later on the CellBrain, so I suspect the controller is on an older version.
1. Check the firmware version under System > About using the old pendant.
2. If it's below 4.5, update to 4.7.2 in Maintenance mode (about 25 minutes, back up .cbp programs first).
3. After the update, plug in the TP-9 and it should pair within a minute.
Line status: keep using the old pendant and the line can keep running until you can schedule the update.
we're on Standard plan, how fast can a tech be here? arm is down and we're losing shifts

On CareGuard Standard, a technician is on site within 48 hours for a line-down ticket.
1. I've marked this as P1 line-down so Dana Okafor's team calls you within 1 hour.
2. Many arm faults can be fixed remotely, so please have someone at the pendant for that call.
3. Send the fault bundle now so we can ship parts before the tech arrives.
Line status: that arm stays down; let us know if any other cells depend on it and we'll help you plan a workaround.
Can you explain the time and materials rates on our last invoice? We don't have a service plan.

Sure. Without a CareGuard plan, work is billed as time and materials.
1. Remote support is $210 per hour.
2. On-site work is $265 per hour plus travel.
3. Parts are billed at list price.
4. If you'd like, I can send a quote for CareGuard Standard ($2,400 per arm per year), which covers remote support and advance replacements.
Line status: this is a billing question only, your line can keep running.
After a minor crash yesterday our AR-200 is placing parts about 3mm off. Collision detection did trigger. What now?

Since collision detection triggered, the arm protected itself, but a 3 mm offset means the calibration needs checking.
1. Run the homing routine, then the Joint Check routine from the teach pendant.
2. Re-teach one reference point and compare; if the offset is the same everywhere, re-check the tool center point.
3. If the offset changes with position, a joint may have slipped; send the fault bundle and we'll review it.
Line status: the line can keep running only if 3 mm is inside your tolerance; otherwise stop that arm until it's recalibrated.
Can one CellBrain run 5 arms? We're adding a fifth AR-60 to the cell.

No, a CellBrain controller runs up to 4 arms.
1. For the fifth AR-60 you'll need a second CellBrain.
2. The two controllers can share the same PLC over the fieldbus.
3. Your account team can quote the controller; firmware should match on both (4.7.2 current).
Line status: your existing 4-arm cell can keep running while you plan the expansion.
RMA got approved at 3:30pm CT today, we're Premier. Will the part ship tonight?

Same-day shipping on Premier applies when the RMA is approved before 14:00 CT, so this one ships first thing tomorrow by overnight freight.
1. Tracking will be emailed as soon as it leaves Harrow Park depot.
2. If the line is fully down, reply and Dana Okafor's team will check whether a technician can bring a part from stock.
Line status: per your ticket the line is running at reduced rate, so it can keep running until the part arrives.
Is support open on Saturdays? Not an emergency, just a question about programs.

The standard support desk is open Monday to Friday, 06:00 to 20:00 Central Time, so a non-urgent question will be picked up Monday morning.
1. Email it to acme.support@example.com and it gets a P3 ticket with a 1 business day response.
2. If a line stops over the weekend, call the 24/7 line-down hotline at 555-0142.
Line status: no impact; the line can keep running.
This is the third time I'm writing about the same T-14 fault. Nobody has called me back and my supervisor is breathing down my neck. Unacceptable.

I'm sorry, you should not have had to write three times. I've merged your tickets and raised it to Dana Okafor, our field service lead, who will call you within 1 hour.
1. If T-14 has hit 3 times in a shift, stop the arm; that's our line-down rule and it gets P1 priority.
2. Please send the latest fault bundle so the technician can bring the right harmonic drive ([AR2-HD-J2] or [AR2-HD-J3]).
3. I'll stay on this ticket personally until it's closed.
Line status: if the fault is recurring, that arm should stop; other cells can keep running.
arm wont home after estop. pendant just says homing blocked

Homing is blocked while the e-stop chain is still open.
1. Twist-release every e-stop button in the cell, including the one on the pendant.
2. Reset the safety circuit on the CellBrain, then try homing again.
3. If it still says blocked, check the pendant for an S-code and send it to us.
Line status: the cell stays stopped until the safety circuit resets; other cells can keep running.
We have an S-03 fault on cell 4 and the PLC guys want to jumper it so we can finish the order. Is that ok?

Please don't jumper it. S-03 is an e-stop chain fault, and S-codes are safety faults that must never be bypassed.
1. Check every e-stop in cell 4 and the wiring to the CellBrain safety input.
2. Look for a door switch or light curtain on the same chain that may be open.
3. If you can't find it, send a fault bundle and we'll walk through the safety circuit with you on a call.
Line status: cell 4 must stay stopped until S-03 clears; cells on separate safety circuits can keep running.
Why is our AR-60 so slow in collaborative mode? Feels like half speed.

That's by design. In collaborative mode the AR-60 cobot is capped at 250 mm/s so it is safe around people.
1. If the cell is fully guarded, you can switch to non-collaborative mode with a risk assessment from your safety team.
2. Otherwise, shorten paths and reduce waiting time to gain cycle time.
Line status: nothing is wrong, the line can keep running as is.
Do I need to back up anything before the 4.7.2 update? We've never done one.

Yes, always back up first.
1. Save every program to USB as a .cbp file (Programs > Export).
2. Export a fault bundle too (Diagnostics > Export Bundle) so we have a baseline.
3. Put the CellBrain in Maintenance mode and run the update; allow about 25 minutes.
4. Run one test cycle on each program before production.
Line status: the cell is offline during the update, so schedule it outside a shift; the line can keep running until then.
4.7.2 broke our vision handshake, can we roll back to 4.6.5?

Yes, but downgrades only go to 4.6.x and they're done with our firmware team.
1. I've assigned this to Marcus Lindqvist, our firmware and CellBrain specialist.
2. Send the fault bundle and the vision system message log so he can confirm the cause.
3. He'll schedule the rollback with you; plan about 25 minutes in Maintenance mode.
Line status: if the vision cell is unreliable, run it in manual-check mode; the rest of the line can keep running.
We want to cancel CareGuard on 2 arms that we're scrapping. How does that work?

We can remove those 2 arms from the plan.
1. Reply with the two arm serial numbers and the date they leave service.
2. Coverage is prorated and the unused part is credited on your next invoice.
3. Make sure there are no open RMAs on those arms, or the cores still need to be returned.
Line status: this is a contract change only; your line can keep running.
We ordered 3 packs of vacuum cups and 2 packs of finger pads, but only the cups arrived.

Sorry for the split delivery. Both ship from Millbrook depot but they sometimes go in separate parcels.
1. The finger pads [GK-PAD-6] are in a second parcel; I'll send you the tracking number.
2. If it hasn't arrived in 2 business days, we'll reship.
Line status: the line can keep running; let us know if the pads are urgent and we'll expedite.
We have no service plan. How much to replace a J3 harmonic drive on site?

Here's a rough estimate for time and materials.
1. Part: joint 3 harmonic drive [AR2-HD-J3] at $3,400 list.
2. Labor: $265 per hour on site, usually 4 to 5 hours for a J3 swap, plus travel.
3. If you'd rather, remote guidance is $210 per hour and your team does the swap.
Line status: if the arm is still throwing T-14, it should stay stopped; other cells can keep running.
Got one T-14 on J2 this morning, cleared it and it's been fine for 2 hours. Anything we should do?

A single cleared T-14 is usually nothing serious.
1. Check that the payload setting on the pendant matches your current tool and part.
2. If you haven't already, run the Joint Check routine.
3. Keep an eye on it; if T-14 comes back 3 times in one shift, open a line-down ticket.
Line status: the line can keep running at 70% speed override while you watch it, and you can go back to full speed if the shift stays clean.
finger pads on the gripkit are worn after 4 months, isn't that under the 6 month warranty

The Gripkit end-effectors have a 6-month warranty, but finger pads and vacuum cups are wear parts and aren't covered.
1. Replacement finger pads [GK-PAD-6] are $54 per 6-pack from Millbrook depot.
2. If the pads wear much faster on one side, check the jaw alignment; that part is covered.
Line status: worn pads can drop parts, but the line can keep running if you swap them at the next break.
Hello, we're looking at adding three more AR-200 arms next quarter. Who do I talk to for a quote?

Thanks for thinking of us for the expansion.
1. I've passed your request to your account team; they'll contact you within 1 business day with a quote.
2. Include your target payload and reach so they can confirm the AR-200 (12 kg, 1,450 mm) fits.
3. Remember each CellBrain runs up to 4 arms, so check your controller count too.
Line status: no impact on production; your line can keep running.
The timestamps in the CellBrain logs are 6 hours off from our plant clock. Makes it hard to match with the PLC.

The CellBrain clock is probably still on UTC.
1. Go to System > Date and Time on the pendant and set your local time zone.
2. Turn on time sync with your plant network time server if you have one.
3. Old log entries keep their original time; only new ones change.
Line status: changing the clock does not stop the robot, so the line can keep running.
Hand guiding on our cobot feels really stiff, like it's fighting us when we teach points

Stiff hand-guiding on the AR-60 is usually a payload setting problem.
1. Make sure the payload on the pendant matches the tool actually mounted; too low makes the arm fight you.
2. Recalibrate the force sensor from Collaborative settings with no load.
3. If it's still stiff, send a fault bundle and we'll check the joint sensors.
Line status: hand-guiding is only for teaching, so the line can keep running in automatic mode.
J2 on one of our AR-200s has started making a grinding sound on fast moves. No faults yet.

Grinding on J2 is an early sign of harmonic drive wear, so let's catch it before it becomes a T-14.
1. Reduce speed override to 70% on that arm to cut the load.
2. Check the grease log; if it's past 4,000 hours, grease J1 to J3 with [AR2-GRS-1].
3. Send a fault bundle and a short audio clip; if it's the drive, we'll plan a [AR2-HD-J2] swap at your next stop.
Line status: the line can keep running at reduced speed for now, but stop the arm if T-14 starts appearing.
We swapped from the vacuum head to a two finger gripper and now the robot is placing parts slightly off. What did we miss?

After a tool change, the tool center point (TCP) and payload need updating.
1. On the pendant, select the tool profile for the two-finger gripper [GK-2F-110] or create one.
2. Teach the TCP using the 4-point method.
3. Set the payload for the gripper plus the part.
Line status: the line can keep running once the new tool profile is active; until then, run that cell slowly and check placements.
We received a CB-FAN-2 but we ordered a CB-PSU-48. Need the power supply urgently.

Sorry, that's our mistake.
1. I've shipped the CellBrain power supply [CB-PSU-48] from Harrow Park depot by overnight freight at no charge.
2. Please return the fan [CB-FAN-2] with the prepaid label we're emailing you.
3. If the controller is down now, tell me and I'll mark the ticket P1 line-down.
Line status: if the PSU has already failed, that controller's cell is stopped until the new one arrives; other cells can keep running.
The replacement encoder arrived with a cracked housing. Box was crushed.

Sorry about that, we'll replace it right away.
1. Take a photo of the box and the part and reply with them.
2. I'm shipping a new encoder [AR2-ENC-04] from Harrow Park depot today and opening a freight claim on our side.
3. Send the damaged one back with the failed original using the same RMA label.
Line status: the affected arm stays stopped until the new encoder is fitted; the rest of the line can keep running.
Teach pendant screen is cracked, operator dropped it. Can we RMA it?

We can repair or replace it, but drop damage isn't covered by warranty.
1. A replacement teach pendant [TP-9] is $2,150 list; we'll quote a screen repair if you'd rather wait.
2. Send the serial number and a photo and I'll open the RMA.
3. Until it arrives, the pendant still works if the touch area is usable; otherwise borrow one from another cell.
Line status: the robot runs in automatic mode without the pendant, so the line can keep running.
When is our quarterly firmware review? We're a Premier customer and haven't had one this year.

Thanks for flagging it. Quarterly firmware reviews are part of CareGuard Premier and are run by Marcus Lindqvist.
1. I've asked Marcus to send you three slots for next week.
2. Have the current firmware version of each CellBrain ready (System > About).
3. Teodora Vance, your customer success manager, will join to cover any missed reviews.
Line status: the review is a call, so the line can keep running.
Can our own maintenance guy replace the CellBrain fan or does it need a tech?

Your own team can do it.
1. Power down and lock out the CellBrain.
2. Remove the 4 screws on the fan cover, unplug the old fan, and fit the new fan [CB-FAN-2].
3. Power up and confirm warning W-22 doesn't come back.
Line status: the cell on that controller is stopped for about 10 minutes during the swap; the rest of the line can keep running.
Every arm in the plant is showing E-07 after this morning's power cut. 11 arms. Help!

This is a common pattern after power loss and is usually fixed by homing.
1. Home each arm from its teach pendant, one at a time.
2. Note any arm where E-07 comes back after homing.
3. Send the fault bundles for those arms only; they may need an encoder [AR2-ENC-04].
4. I've opened this as a P1 line-down ticket so Dana Okafor's team can call you within the hour if it doesn't clear.
Line status: each arm can rejoin the line as soon as it homes cleanly.
I want to escalate. Who is in charge of field service? Our tech hasn't shown up and the 8 hours are almost up.

You're right to escalate. Our field service and line-down lead is Dana Okafor, and I've forwarded your ticket to her directly.
1. She'll call you within 1 hour with the technician's exact ETA.
2. As a Premier account, if we miss the 8-hour window, Teodora Vance will follow up on the service credit.
3. Keep the fault bundle handy for the technician.
Line status: per your ticket the line is down; we'll confirm what can run as soon as the tech has assessed it.
Our safety auditor wants documentation on the AR-60 safety skin. Do you have something?

Yes, we can send the safety documentation pack for the AR-60 cobot.
1. Reply with the cobot serial numbers so we send the right revision.
2. The pack covers the safety skin pads [AR6-SKIN-02], S-code list and collaborative speed limit of 250 mm/s.
3. If the auditor wants a call, Dana Okafor's team can join.
Line status: no impact; the line can keep running.
We put a third party gripper on our AR-200. Will you still support the robot?

Yes, we still support the arm and the CellBrain.
1. We can't troubleshoot the third-party gripper itself.
2. Make sure its weight is set correctly in the payload, since an incorrect payload causes torque fault T-14.
3. If a fault is caused by the gripper, the repair may not be covered by warranty.
Line status: the line can keep running with the third-party tool.
Tech came today and swapped the J3 drive, robot running great. Thanks to everyone, you can close the ticket.

Great news, thanks for letting us know.
1. Please return the old harmonic drive [AR2-HD-J3] within 15 calendar days using the prepaid label so it isn't billed.
2. Run the Joint Check routine once a day for the next week as a precaution.
3. I'm closing the ticket now; reply anytime to reopen it.
Line status: the line is back to full speed and can keep running.
What are our first-response SLAs for each ticket priority?

Acme Robotics first-response SLAs:
1. P1 line-down ticket (line stopped): 1 hour, 24/7.
2. P2 degraded (line running with a fault or at reduced rate): 4 hours, within support hours.
3. P3 standard or how-to: 1 business day (8 support hours).
Support hours are Monday to Friday, 06:00 to 20:00 Central Time; the line-down hotline 555-0142 is always open.
Customer site already has 2 open advance replacements and wants a third. Can I approve it?

No, not on your own. The limit is 2 open advance replacements per site.
1. A third needs approval from the account's customer success manager (Teodora Vance for Premier accounts).
2. Alternatively, once the customer returns one of the open cores, you can ship without approval.
3. Prepare the RMA with the fault bundle so it ships as soon as it's approved.
How many days does a customer have to send back the failed part on an RMA?

15 calendar days from receiving the advance replacement.
1. They use the prepaid label in the replacement box.
2. Gripkit parts go to Millbrook depot; everything else goes to Harrow Park depot.
3. If the core isn't received in 15 days, the replacement is billed at list price.
What's the price difference between CareGuard Standard and Premier?

Standard is $2,400 per arm per year and Premier is $5,800 per arm per year, a difference of $3,400 per arm.
1. Standard: remote support, next-business-day advance replacement, on-site tech within 48 hours on line-down tickets.
2. Premier: on-site tech within 8 hours, same-day shipping if the RMA is approved before 14:00 CT, loaner CellBrain up to 30 days, quarterly firmware reviews, named customer success manager.
Which depot ships Gripkit spares?
Millbrook depot ships Gripkit end-effectors and spares by parcel, and Gripkit returns go back to Millbrook. Harrow Park depot handles arm parts, CellBrain controllers and TP-9 pendants.
A Standard plan customer is asking for a loaner CellBrain. Is that allowed?

No. Loaner CellBrain controllers are a Premier-only benefit, for a maximum of 30 days.
1. Offer the Standard advance replacement, which ships next business day after RMA approval.
2. If the customer wants loaners in future, quote the upgrade to Premier ($5,800 per arm per year).
What are our time and materials rates for customers without a plan?

Without a CareGuard plan:
1. Remote support: $210 per hour.
2. On-site work: $265 per hour plus travel.
3. Parts: list price.
Training is separate: $1,450 per on-site day, and CellBrain Operator 101 is $350 per seat for non-plan customers.
Which firmware does the TP-9 pendant need?
The TP-9 teach pendant needs firmware rail 4.5 or later on the CellBrain. If a customer reports a TP-9 stuck on connecting, check the controller version first and recommend the current stable, 4.7.2.
When does support for firmware 4.6 end?

Rail 4.6.x is supported until 31 March 2027. Current stable is 4.7.2. Rail 3.x is already end-of-life with no patches. Downgrades are only allowed to 4.6.x and must go through Marcus Lindqvist on the firmware team.
What's the warranty on each Acme product?

Warranty from ship date:
1. AR-200 six-axis arm: 24 months.
2. AR-60 cobot: 12 months.
3. CellBrain controller: 36 months.
4. Gripkit end-effectors: 6 months, with vacuum cups and finger pads excluded as wear parts.
Crash damage with collision detection disabled is never covered.
When does a T-14 turn into a line-down ticket?

When torque fault T-14 repeats 3 times in one shift.
1. Below that, the customer clears it, checks payload, runs Joint Check and resumes at 70% speed override.
2. At 3 in a shift, the arm stops, the ticket goes to P1, and we usually ship a harmonic drive ([AR2-HD-J2] or [AR2-HD-J3]).
3. Always tell the customer whether the line can keep running.
What's the cutoff for same-day shipping on Premier?

The RMA must be approved before 14:00 Central Time. After that it ships the next morning by overnight freight from Harrow Park depot (or by parcel from Millbrook for Gripkit). Standard customers always get next-business-day shipping.
Where does the customer find the fault bundle export?

On the CellBrain screen or teach pendant: Diagnostics > Export Bundle. It saves a .cbx file to USB with the controller serial in the file name. It doesn't stop the robot, so they can do it while the line runs.
Who handles firmware escalations and downgrade requests?

Marcus Lindqvist, our firmware and CellBrain specialist. He owns all downgrades (only to 4.6.x) and runs the Premier quarterly firmware reviews. Assign the ticket to him with the customer's fault bundle attached.
What's the format of an RMA number?
RMA-AR- followed by 4 digits, for example RMA-AR-4471. The RMA desk issues it after the fault bundle and serial number are received. Priya Halvorsen leads the RMA desk.
Can a customer keep the line running with an S-code active?

No, not the affected cell. S-codes (S-01 to S-19) are safety faults covering the e-stop chain, safety skin and light curtains.
1. That cell must stay stopped until the fault clears.
2. Never advise jumpering or bypassing.
3. Other cells may keep running if they are on separate safety circuits.
Customer crashed an AR-200 with collision detection off. Do we cover it under Premier?

No. Crash damage while collision detection was disabled is excluded under every plan, Premier included. Parts are billed at list price (for example [AR2-HD-J2] at $3,850). Premier labor and the 8-hour on-site response still apply.
How often should customers grease AR-200 joints and with what?
Every 4,000 operating hours on J1 to J3, using one joint grease cartridge [AR2-GRS-1] per joint ($45 each). The arm must be locked out, so recommend doing it during a planned stop.
What's the max payload and reach of the AR-60 compared to the AR-200?
AR-60 cobot: 5 kg payload, 900 mm reach, collaborative speed capped at 250 mm/s. AR-200 six-axis arm: 12 kg payload, 1,450 mm reach. A CellBrain can run up to 4 arms of either type.
Who is the escalation contact when a Premier on-site visit misses the 8-hour window?
Escalate to Dana Okafor, the field service and line-down lead, for the technician ETA. Teodora Vance, the customer success manager for Premier accounts, handles the follow-up and any service credit.

prompt.content: Got T-14 on the welding cell arm, joint 3. First time today. What do I do?

chosen:
A first T-14 on J3 is usually recoverable.
1. Check the payload setting on the teach pendant matches the torch and cable package.
2. Clear the fault and run the Joint Check routine.
3. Resume at 70% speed override and watch the next cycles.
4. If it repeats 3 times this shift, call it in as a line-down ticket; the likely part is [AR2-HD-J3].
Line status: you can keep the line running at 70% override. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Torque faults can happen for many reasons. Try restarting the robot and see if the problem goes away. If it keeps happening, contact support and we will look into it.

prompt.content: our cobot keeps stopping with S-12 when nobody is touching it

chosen:
S-12 with no contact usually means a damaged or loose safety skin pad.
1. Inspect each pad for cracks and check that every pad is seated.
2. Send a fault bundle (CellBrain > Diagnostics > Export Bundle) so we can see which pad is triggering.
3. We'll ship a replacement safety skin pad [AR6-SKIN-02] from Harrow Park depot.
Line status: that cobot's cell must stay stopped while S-12 is active; don't bypass the skin. Other cells can keep running. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: It sounds like the sensor is too sensitive. You could lower the sensitivity in the settings so it stops tripping, and the cobot should go back to normal operation.

prompt.content: Can you send me a replacement encoder? Arm 4 has E-07 and homing didn't fix it.

chosen:
Yes. If E-07 survives homing, the encoder needs replacing.
1. Export the fault bundle and reply with it and the arm serial.
2. I'll open the RMA and ship encoder [AR2-ENC-04] from Harrow Park depot.
3. Return the old encoder within 15 calendar days using the prepaid label.
Line status: arm 4 stays stopped until the new encoder is fitted; the rest of the line can keep running. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Sure, I can help with that. Please let us know your address and we'll get a part out to you as soon as possible.

prompt.content: how much is a new teach pendant

chosen:
A new TP-9 teach pendant [TP-9] is $2,150 list.
1. It needs firmware rail 4.5 or later on the CellBrain.
2. If you only need a cable, the 5 m cable [TP-9-CBL5] is $180.
Line status: the robot runs in automatic mode without a pendant, so the line can keep running while you order. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Pricing depends on several factors. I'd recommend reaching out to your sales representative for an accurate quote on a teach pendant.

prompt.content: Our CellBrain is on 4.4 and someone said we should update. Is it safe to do during the shift?

chosen:
Don't update during the shift. Firmware updates need the CellBrain in Maintenance mode.
1. Back up all programs as .cbp files.
2. Schedule about 25 minutes per controller outside production.
3. Update to the current stable, 4.7.2.
Line status: the line can keep running on 4.4 until your planned stop. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Yes, updating firmware is generally safe. Just start the update from the settings menu and let it finish. It's a good idea to keep your software up to date.

prompt.content: Need a quote for vacuum cups, 5 packs.

chosen:
Here's your quote.
1. Gripkit 40 mm vacuum cups [GK-VAC-40], 5 x 10-packs at $68 = $340.
2. Ships by parcel from Millbrook depot, usually next business day.
3. Vacuum cups are wear parts, so they're billed even under warranty.
Line status: no impact on the line; it can keep running. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Thanks for your interest! The vacuum cups are available. Please place the order through the portal and it will ship soon.

prompt.content: Line is down, controller shows nothing at all, no lights. It's 2am.

chosen:
You've reached the 24/7 line-down hotline and this is now a P1 ticket.
1. Check the cabinet breaker and the mains feed to the CellBrain.
2. If mains is present but the PSU LED is off, the likely part is the 48 V supply [CB-PSU-48].
3. Dana Okafor's on-call team will call you within 1 hour to confirm and start the advance replacement.
Line status: the cell on that controller cannot run until it powers up; other cells on their own controllers can keep running. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Sorry to hear that. Our support team is available during business hours and will get back to you as soon as possible. In the meantime, try turning the controller off and on again.

prompt.content: is crash damage covered by our premier plan? collision detect was off

chosen:
Unfortunately not. Crash damage with collision detection disabled is excluded under every plan, Premier included.
1. Parts are billed at list price; for example a J2 drive [AR2-HD-J2] is $3,850.
2. Premier still covers labor and the 8-hour on-site response.
3. Re-enable collision detection before restarting.
Line status: the crashed arm should stay stopped until it's inspected; other cells can keep running. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Premier is our most comprehensive plan, so it should cover most kinds of damage. Send us the details and we'll take care of it.

prompt.content: We're adding a 4th arm to our CellBrain. Do we need a second controller?

chosen:
No, a CellBrain runs up to 4 arms, so a 4th arm fits.
1. Make sure the new arm and controller are on the same firmware (4.7.2 current).
2. Set the payload and TCP for the new arm's tool before running.
3. A 5th arm would need a second CellBrain.
Line status: the existing 3 arms can keep running while you install the 4th; only the new arm's area needs to be locked out. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Every setup is different. It depends on your configuration, so you may want to consult with an engineer before adding more arms.

prompt.content: Where do I send back a Gripkit two-finger gripper under RMA?

chosen:
Gripkit returns go to Millbrook depot.
1. Use the prepaid label in the replacement box; it's already addressed to Millbrook.
2. Put the RMA number (RMA-AR-####) on the outside of the box.
3. Ship the old gripper [GK-2F-110] within 15 calendar days to avoid a list-price charge.
Line status: once the replacement gripper is fitted, the line can keep running. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Please send it back to our main warehouse. The address should be on your paperwork.

prompt.content: We have 1 RMA open and need another one for a PSU. Any problem?

chosen:
No problem. You'll have 2 open advance replacements, which is the per-site limit.
1. Send the fault bundle and controller serial.
2. I'll ship the power supply [CB-PSU-48] from Harrow Park depot.
3. A third open replacement would need approval from your customer success manager, so return the first core when you can.
Line status: the cell on the failed controller is down until the PSU arrives; other cells can keep running. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: No problem at all, you can open as many RMAs as you need. Just submit the request.

prompt.content: What is the warranty on the CellBrain? Ours is 2.5 years old and the fan died.

chosen:
The CellBrain controller has a 36-month warranty, so at 2.5 years you're covered.
1. Open an RMA with the controller serial and we'll ship a fan [CB-FAN-2] from Harrow Park depot.
2. Your own team can swap it in about 10 minutes with the controller locked out.
Line status: until the swap, the line can keep running, but watch for warning W-22; the cell stops if it becomes a temperature fault. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Most of our products come with a standard warranty. Let us check your purchase records and get back to you.

prompt.content: Robot drops parts sometimes after we changed the Gripkit fingers.

chosen:
Dropped parts after a finger change usually means the pads or the payload/TCP need adjusting.
1. Check the new finger pads [GK-PAD-6] are seated and not glazed.
2. Update the tool profile on the teach pendant: payload and TCP for the new fingers.
3. Check the quick-change plate [GK-QC-1] has no play.
Line status: the line can keep running at reduced speed until the tool profile is fixed. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Try increasing the grip force. That usually fixes dropping issues. Let us know if you need anything else.

prompt.content: can a tech come tomorrow? we're on standard, robot is down

chosen:
On CareGuard Standard, the on-site window for a line-down ticket is 48 hours, so tomorrow is possible.
1. I've opened this as a P1 line-down ticket and Dana Okafor's team will call you within 1 hour.
2. Send the fault bundle so the tech can bring the right parts.
3. Many faults can be fixed remotely on that call, which may be faster than waiting for a visit.
Line status: the down robot stays stopped; tell us which cells depend on it and we'll help you keep the rest running. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: We'll try our best to send someone as soon as we can. Please be patient while we arrange a technician.

prompt.content: The arm in cell 6 sounds rough on J3 and we're at 4,300 hours. Related?

chosen:
Very likely. The grease interval is 4,000 operating hours, so J1 to J3 are overdue.
1. At your next stop, lock out the arm and grease J1 to J3 with one cartridge [AR2-GRS-1] per joint.
2. Run the Joint Check routine afterwards.
3. If J3 still sounds rough, send a fault bundle; it may be early wear on [AR2-HD-J3].
Line status: the line can keep running at 70% speed override until the grease job. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Robots can make some noise as they age, it's usually nothing to worry about. Keep an eye on it.

prompt.content: We want to downgrade to 4.6. How?

chosen:
Downgrades are possible to 4.6.x only and are done with our firmware team.
1. I've assigned your ticket to Marcus Lindqvist, our firmware and CellBrain specialist.
2. Back up all programs (.cbp) and send a fault bundle so he can check compatibility.
3. He'll book a slot with you; plan about 25 minutes per controller in Maintenance mode.
Line status: the line can keep running on the current version until the rollback slot. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: You can download older firmware versions from the internet and install them yourself using a USB drive.

prompt.content: does premier get same day shipping always?

chosen:
Same-day shipping on Premier applies when the RMA is approved before 14:00 Central Time.
1. Approved before 14:00 CT: ships the same day by overnight freight from Harrow Park depot.
2. Approved after 14:00 CT: ships first thing the next morning.
3. To beat the cutoff, send the fault bundle and serial with your first message.
Line status: no impact on your line from this question; it can keep running. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Yes, Premier customers always get same-day shipping on every order.

prompt.content: Our C-31 faults started after an electrician worked on the cabinet. Ideas?

chosen:
That timing points to the fieldbus wiring.
1. Check the fieldbus connectors at the CellBrain and the PLC were reseated fully.
2. Confirm the bus terminator wasn't removed or moved during the work.
3. Look for the fieldbus cable now running next to power cables; move it away to cut noise.
4. If C-31 continues, send a fault bundle for Marcus Lindqvist to check timing.
Line status: other cells can keep running; the affected cell runs with interruptions until it's fixed. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: C-31 is a communication error. Please contact your electrician to fix it, as this is not an issue with our robot.

prompt.content: We need the line running for a big order tonight. The AR-60 has a cracked skin pad but works. Can we just tape it?

chosen:
Please don't tape it. A cracked pad can stop the safety skin from detecting contact, and that's a safety risk.
1. Order a safety skin pad [AR6-SKIN-02] ($390); I can mark it urgent from Harrow Park depot.
2. If the cell is fully guarded with no people inside, your safety team may run it in non-collaborative mode after a risk assessment.
3. Otherwise keep that cobot stopped until the pad is replaced.
Line status: the rest of the line can keep running; this cobot should not run in collaborative mode with a cracked pad. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Taping it should be fine as a temporary fix. Just make sure to replace it when you get a chance.

prompt.content: Our invoice says $3,850 for a part we never got.

chosen:
Let's sort that out. $3,850 is the list price of the J2 harmonic drive [AR2-HD-J2].
1. Reply with the invoice number and any RMA number on it.
2. I'll ask Priya Halvorsen on the RMA desk to check the shipping record from Harrow Park depot.
3. If it never shipped, the invoice is cancelled and you get a credit note within 2 business days.
Line status: billing only; your line can keep running. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: We apologize for any confusion. Invoices are handled by our billing department, please contact them directly.

prompt.content: How do I stop the cobot being so slow?

chosen:
In collaborative mode the AR-60 cobot is capped at 250 mm/s for safety, so it will feel slow.
1. Shorten the paths and remove unneeded waypoints.
2. If the cell is fully guarded, your safety team can approve non-collaborative mode after a risk assessment.
3. Check payload is set correctly, since a wrong payload also slows moves.
Line status: nothing is faulty; the line can keep running. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: You can increase the speed in the settings menu. Just turn the speed slider up to the maximum.

prompt.content: is there a course for new operators?

chosen:
Yes, two options.
1. CellBrain Operator 101: a remote course, free for CareGuard customers ($350 per seat otherwise).
2. On-site training: $1,450 per day for up to 8 trainees.
3. We recommend Operator 101 first, then an on-site day for hands-on work at your cells.
Line status: training doesn't affect production; the line can keep running. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: We have lots of resources available online. Check out our website for videos and documentation.

prompt.content: Ticket's been open 5 hours on a line-down. Where is everyone??

chosen:
I'm sorry, a line-down ticket should get a first response within 1 hour. I've escalated it to Dana Okafor, our field service and line-down lead.
1. She'll call you within the hour with a plan and technician ETA.
2. Please send the fault bundle now (CellBrain > Diagnostics > Export Bundle) so parts can ship right away.
3. I'll keep this ticket on my desk until it's resolved.
Line status: the affected cell stays down; tell us which other cells are running and we'll protect those first. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Thank you for your patience. We are experiencing high ticket volumes right now. Someone will be with you shortly.

prompt.content: Do we need to do anything with the old part after the tech swapped it?

chosen:
Yes, please send it back.
1. Pack the old part in the replacement box and use the prepaid label.
2. Arm and controller parts go to Harrow Park depot; Gripkit parts go to Millbrook depot.
3. It must arrive within 15 calendar days, or the replacement is billed at list price.
Line status: the repair is done, so the line can keep running. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: You can dispose of the old part however you like, or keep it as a spare.

prompt.content: Joint 2 T-14 three times since midnight. Can we keep running at slow speed?

chosen:
Three T-14 faults in one shift means we stop the arm; it's our line-down rule.
1. Stop the arm and keep the CellBrain powered.
2. Send the fault bundle; I've raised this to a P1 line-down ticket.
3. The likely part is the J2 harmonic drive [AR2-HD-J2]; we'll start the advance replacement as soon as the bundle confirms it.
Line status: no, that arm should not keep running, even at slow speed. Other cells can keep running. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Running at slow speed should be okay for now. Keep an eye on it and let us know if it gets worse.

prompt.content: We moved the CellBrain into the paint shop and now it shows W-22 all the time.

chosen:
W-22 is the over-temperature warning, so the new location is probably too hot or dusty.
1. Clean the intake grille and check the fan [CB-FAN-2] is spinning.
2. Give the cabinet more clearance or add filtered ventilation.
3. If the fan is noisy or slow, replace it; it's a 10-minute swap.
Line status: W-22 is a warning, so the line can keep running, but the controller will stop the cell if it reaches a temperature fault. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: That warning is not important, you can ignore it.

prompt.content: Hi, the gripper fingers on our GK-2F-110 are chipped after a bad pick. Which part do we order?

chosen:
For chipped finger surfaces, order the finger pads [GK-PAD-6], $54 per 6-pack from Millbrook depot.
1. Swap the pads and run 10 open-close cycles from the pendant.
2. If the jaw itself is chipped, send a photo; the gripper [GK-2F-110] may need repair.
3. Pads are wear parts, so they're billed even under the 6-month Gripkit warranty.
Line status: the line can keep running at reduced speed until the new pads arrive. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: You'll probably need a new gripper. Please contact sales for a quote.

prompt.content: New TP-9 won't pair with the controller, old pendant fine.

chosen:
The TP-9 needs firmware rail 4.5 or later on the CellBrain.
1. Check the version under System > About with the old pendant.
2. If it's below 4.5, back up your .cbp programs and update to 4.7.2 in Maintenance mode (about 25 minutes).
3. Then connect the TP-9 [TP-9] again; it should pair within a minute.
Line status: keep using the old pendant and the line can keep running until the update. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: The new pendant probably needs a firmware update on the controller. Update the controller software and try again, it should work after that.

prompt.content: Our e-stop on cell 2 keeps tripping by itself, S-03. Can maintenance jump it out for today?

chosen:
Please don't jump it. S-03 is an e-stop chain fault and safety circuits must never be bypassed.
1. Check each e-stop in cell 2 for a loose contact block.
2. Inspect the e-stop cable to the CellBrain safety input for damage, especially at moving guards.
3. If you can't find it, send a fault bundle and we'll trace the circuit with you on a call.
Line status: cell 2 must stay stopped until S-03 clears; cells on separate safety circuits can keep running. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: We don't recommend bypassing safety devices, but it's your decision. If you do, make sure to restore it as soon as possible. A loose wire is the usual cause.

prompt.content: hi we bought an AR-60 11 months ago, joint makes clicking noise. warranty?

chosen:
Yes, the AR-60 cobot has a 12-month warranty, so at 11 months you're covered.
1. Send a fault bundle and a short video with the sound.
2. We'll open the RMA quickly so it's logged inside the warranty period.
3. Parts ship from Harrow Park depot; on Standard, next business day.
Line status: if there are no faults, the line can keep running at reduced speed while we diagnose it. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: The AR-60 has a warranty. Please send us your proof of purchase and we'll review whether this issue qualifies.

prompt.content: What's the 1-hour SLA thing? Does it apply to my question about reports?

chosen:
The 1-hour first response applies only to P1 line-down tickets, when a line is stopped.
1. A question about reports is a P3 standard ticket: first response within 1 business day.
2. If your line is running but with a fault, that's P2: 4 hours.
3. Our standard desk hours are Monday to Friday, 06:00 to 20:00 Central Time.
Line status: your line isn't affected, so it can keep running. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: We aim to respond to all tickets as quickly as possible. Your question has been received and will be answered soon.

prompt.content: Robot homes fine but E-07 comes back after an hour or so.

chosen:
An E-07 that returns after a clean home points to a failing encoder.
1. Export the fault bundle right after the next E-07 so the log shows which joint.
2. We'll open an RMA for an encoder [AR2-ENC-04] and ship it from Harrow Park depot.
3. Until then, re-home after each E-07.
Line status: the line can keep running with re-homing, but expect stops on that arm until the encoder is replaced. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Encoder errors are usually caused by electrical noise. Check your grounding and see if it goes away.

prompt.content: we're installing a heavier gripper, 3.5kg, on the AR-60. parts are 2kg. ok?

chosen:
That's 5.5 kg total, which is over the AR-60 cobot's 5 kg max payload.
1. Use a lighter gripper, for example a Gripkit two-finger gripper [GK-2F-110] mounted on the quick-change plate [GK-QC-1].
2. Or move the job to an AR-200, which handles 12 kg.
3. Running over payload will cause torque faults and wear on the joints.
Line status: keep the current gripper on and the line can keep running until you've chosen the new setup. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: That should be fine. The AR-60 can handle a range of grippers. Set the payload and test it.

prompt.content: Got a replacement PSU but it's the wrong voltage label?

chosen:
Let's check before you install anything.
1. The correct part is the CellBrain 48 V power supply [CB-PSU-48]; please send a photo of the label.
2. If it's not 48 V, don't install it. I'll ship the correct one from Harrow Park depot today.
3. Return the wrong part with the prepaid label we'll email you.
Line status: the cell on that controller stays down until the right PSU is fitted; other cells can keep running. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: All our power supplies are compatible, so you can install it anyway.

prompt.content: How long does a firmware update take? We have 3 controllers.

chosen:
Plan about 25 minutes per CellBrain, so roughly 75 minutes for 3 controllers, plus testing.
1. Back up all programs as .cbp files first.
2. Put each CellBrain into Maintenance mode and update one at a time to 4.7.2.
3. Run a test cycle on each before starting the next.
Line status: each cell is offline during its update, so schedule it outside production; the line can keep running until then. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: It doesn't take very long. You can do all three at once in a few minutes.

prompt.content: Arm stopped mid-cycle, pendant says T-14 J3, but we only changed the program, not the tool.

chosen:
A new program can cause T-14 if it adds faster or longer moves with a heavy load.
1. Check that the program is using the right tool profile and payload.
2. Clear the fault, run Joint Check, and resume at 70% speed override.
3. Look for new moves with sharp accelerations near full reach and smooth them out.
4. If T-14 repeats 3 times this shift, stop the arm and call it in; the likely part is [AR2-HD-J3].
Line status: after one T-14, the line can keep running at 70% override. {{SIGNOFF}}
rejected: Please revert to your old program. If the issue continues, open a support ticket with more details.
